payload.title: Councillors agreed a draft policy and asked for it to go out to consultation
payload.summary: On 5 March 2026 the Licensing committee went through a redrafted licensing policy. Members changed the wording on licence conditions themselves and asked officers to look again at two points during the consultation. They then resolved to recommend the draft to Cabinet, and to recommend that Cabinet start a 12-week public consultation. This was a decision to ask the public, not a decision on the policy itself — that comes later, at full council.
detail: Paragraphs 7.1 and 7.4 were to change from 'necessary and proportionate' to 'appropriate and proportionate'. Officers said this gives the council more discretion when imposing conditions.
Officers were asked to explore wording on making signage at premises easier to read.
They were also asked to look at how long premises must keep logbooks and who may inspect them.

A member argued for stronger safeguards for women and girls, including anti-spiking measures, door supervision and clearer ways for victims and staff to report problems. This was left to be picked up through the consultation.
The legal adviser noted that adopting the 'agent of change' principle was unusual for a licensing policy, though the national framework includes it.
The report proposed consulting from 11 May to 7 August 2026. The consultation actually ran a week later, from 18 May to 9 August.
